title: A scene can close its loop and still jerk
idea: Scrub a synthetic Gaussian scene under Fourier-periodic, endpoint-only and drifting motion. Inspect analytic position/velocity seam errors separately from camera closure.
controls: Phase, harmonics, period, deformation mode, camera path/orbit; PNG/GIF export in square or wide format.
misconception: Matching the first and last rendered frames does not ensure a smooth 3D loop; a mathematically closed loop can still move implausibly.
connection: OuroWorld · 8 Oct 2026. Implemented analytic teaching lab; not OuroWorld inference, learned deformation or an evaluation.

title: One pixel of error depends on the camera
idea: Quantize a synthetic Gaussian scene and compare original and decoded centers and footprints. Show measured screen displacement alongside an analytic position bound; refine a toy bit stream in discrete valid steps.
controls: Position precision, pixel tolerance, camera distance, focal length, frustum half-angle, declared near plane; separate footprint/color perturbations; proposed PNG/GIF export.
misconception: A good average image score does not bound each splat. Parameter guarantees do not automatically bound the final composited image, and a guarantee can stop applying outside its declared camera domain.
connection: PLEDGE · 13 Oct 2026, discovered 14 Oct. Proposed analytic teaching lab, not its codec. Keep pruning loss, missing primitives and quantization error separate; do not invent real compressed-byte counts.
audience: 3D artists, graphics engineers and ML practitioners
recommendation: Best new pairing. Extend the existing Gaussian projection teaching machinery with camera-domain and quantization controls.

title: The sound moves the right way but misses the target
idea: Animate a small bank of damped sinusoids beside a spectrum and decay envelope. Compare requested frequency/decay with achieved values when size and thickness change together; toggle known versus hidden thickness.
controls: Size, thickness ratio, damping, excitation, target tolerances and paired random seed; proposed audio audition and PNG/GIF export.
misconception: A monotonic slider response is not calibrated control. A model can rank targets correctly while missing their values, and measured effective damping is not necessarily material loss.
connection: PhysicsSliders · 13 Oct 2026, discovered 14 Oct. Proposed analytic resonator, not trained flow-model output or a reproduction of the paper's success rate.
audience: Sound designers, filmmakers and ML engineers
recommendation: Use a synthetic counterexample to separate direction, calibration and two-target success. Do not label invented samples as paper audio.

title: Separate tracks without changing the original mix
idea: Show two captioned stem streams and a protected mix as an attention matrix. Toggle the forbidden stem-to-mix edge and mix-token LoRA gate, tracing how information could alter the scene stream.
controls: Attention edges, stem-only adapter gate, per-stem captions, aligned versus concatenated time positions, clean versus noisy mix conditioning.
misconception: Blocking an attention edge alone does not freeze a stream if shared adapter updates still alter its token projections.
connection: SepGen · 8 Oct 2026. Proposed synthetic token calculation; no claimed audio separation score or generated waveform. Actual source timing and audio quality need the model.
audience: Audio/video model engineers and creative technologists

title: Why moving noise makes it fade
idea: Track a pixel footprint across a seeded noise grid. Compare ordinary averaging with variance-normalized projection; show histogram and cross-frame correlation.
controls: Zoom, footprint shape, camera motion, sample count, histogram bins, normalization; propose PNG/GIF/MP4 exports.
misconception: Warping standard Gaussian noise does not automatically preserve its variance. Unit variance also does not imply independent pixels.
connection: Tabula Rasa · 8 Oct 2026. Proposed analytic teaching model, not its renderer or generated footage.

title: An edit needs two scorecards
idea: Manipulate a synthetic scene and soundtrack. Plot intended change versus collateral change, then compare arithmetic and harmonic scoring.
controls: Object edit, background drift, sound timing, preservation, judge uncertainty; propose PNG/GIF exports.
misconception: An unchanged clip preserves everything but performs no edit; a convincing new clip can ignore preservation.
connection: CrossEdit · 7 Oct 2026. Proposed synthetic illustration of editing evaluation; no model output or reproduced benchmark.

title: The future you can still change
idea: Animate user and assistant token lanes, separating played audio from tentative future frames. Trigger an interruption and inspect discarded predictions and compute calls.
controls: Prediction horizon, confidence threshold, interruption timing, Listen/Speak policy; propose PNG/GIF exports.
misconception: Fewer model calls do not necessarily mean lower response latency or unchanged speech quality.
connection: DiffuPlex · 8 Oct 2026. Proposed scheduling schematic; synthetic tokens and timing, not a speech-model reproduction.

title: 3B active does not mean a 3B-sized model
idea: Animate tokens routing through an expert bank while separating stored weights, active computation and attention-cache growth. Plot calculated memory components beside the routing view.
controls: Sequence length, weight/cache precision, hypothetical expert count and active experts, full-attention fraction; proposed PNG/GIF export.
misconception: Sparse activation lowers work per token but does not erase inactive expert weights. A smaller full-attention fraction reduces one growing memory component, not every memory cost.
connection: Drama 3 · 13 Oct 2026. Its card describes 35B total / about 3B active parameters and hybrid attention. Proposed analytic model with explicit assumptions, not measured VRAM or Drama 3 inference.
audience: ML engineers and creators comparing self-hosted voice options
status: Proposed; no new visual implemented in this delta
recommendation: Use separate weight and cache axes; show an overhead bucket and avoid claiming a hardware requirement from this toy alone.
